subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Cold Brew vs. Iced Coffee
description: A fast breakdown of Cold Brew vs. Iced Coffee for builders.

hook.text: Cold brew and iced coffee taste completely different—even when made from the same beans.

buildup.text: Iced coffee is hot-brewed coffee poured over ice. It retains bright acidity from hot extraction.

discovery.text: Cold brew steeps grounds in cold water for 12–24 hours. Low temperature extracts fewer acids and less bitterness.

twist.text: Cold brew is a concentrate—typically 2x strength—meant to be diluted with water or milk.

climax.text: Japanese flash brew splits the difference: hot water drips onto ice, preserving aroma while chilling instantly.

punchline.text: Same beans, different physics, different drink entirely.

quiz.question: Why is cold brew less acidic than iced coffee?
options: Low temperature extracts fewer acid compounds

details.summary: Cold brew steeps coarse grounds in cold water for 12 to 24 hours, producing a smooth, low-acid concentrate. Iced coffee is regular hot-brewed coffee poured over ice, retaining its brightness and acidity. They are fundamentally different drinks despite both being served cold.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding the difference helps consumers choose the cold coffee style they prefer and helps cafes communicate their offerings accurately.
takeaways: Cold brew steeps in cold water for 12 to 24 hours
Iced coffee is hot-brewed coffee cooled with ice
Cold brew is smoother and less acidic than iced coffee

faq.question: Why is cold brew less acidic than regular coffee?
faq.answer: Cold water extracts different compounds than hot water. Many acids that dissolve readily in hot water are barely extracted at low temperatures. This produces a coffee with up to 67 percent less acidity, resulting in a smoother, sweeter taste profile.

faq.question: Does cold brew have more caffeine than hot coffee?
faq.answer: Cold brew concentrate has more caffeine per ounce than regular coffee because of the high coffee-to-water ratio. However, it is typically diluted before drinking. A served glass of cold brew and a cup of hot coffee usually contain similar caffeine levels.
